title: Mode
summary: The value that repeats most often in the recent window, drawn only when some value actually repeats, marking prices the market keeps returning to.
descriptionHtml:
The Mode study counts how many times each distinct value of the source appears in the last Period bars and plots the one that appears most often. Values are compared exactly, so two closes count as the same only when they are equal to the last decimal.

When two or more values share the highest count, the winner is the one met first while walking back from the current bar, which is the most recent of the tied values. When every value in the window is different there is no mode, and the study draws nothing on that bar.

Early bars use as many bars as exist rather than waiting for a full window, and absent values are skipped.
howToReadHtml:
A mode that appears and holds the same value over many bars shows a price the instrument keeps settling at, often a round number or a level where orders cluster. Gaps in the line are bars where no value repeated in the window, which is the usual case for a finely priced instrument with a short period.

The study is most useful on a coarse source or a longer period, where repeats are common. On a source with many decimals it may draw very little, which is an honest answer rather than a fault.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The series whose repeated values are counted. A coarser series repeats more often.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How many recent bars are counted. A longer period finds more repeats and changes less often.

faq.q: Why are there gaps in the line?
faq.html: On those bars every value in the window was different, so no value is more common than another and there is no mode to draw.
The one met first walking back from the current bar, which is the most recent of the tied values. A later value has to repeat strictly more often to replace it.
A longer period gives repeats more chance to appear. With a short period on a finely priced instrument the line will be mostly empty.

related.title: Percentile
related.summary: The value at a chosen percentile of the source over a rolling window, drawn on the price chart, interpolated between the two nearest ranks.

related.title: Median
related.summary: The middle value of the source over a rolling window, a centre line that a single outlier bar cannot drag around the way it drags a mean.

related.title: Polynomial Fitting (POLYFIT)
related.summary: Fits a least-squares polynomial of the chosen degree to the recent window and plots the fitted curve's value at the current bar.
